person.summary: Hey there. I am a software developer based in New York, currently at Chronograph Private Equity, where I lead the development of AI tools that automate the extraction of unstructured data from our clients.

writing.heading: Soft Skills & Testimonials
paragraphs: Working in software is not an individual sport. It requires empathy, communication, and collaboration. Strong technical skills are important, but the ability to listen, adapt, and work effectively with others is what truly drives impactful software development and team growth.

In that vein, I believe that soft skills are a key to being a force multiplier. Whether through mentorship, clear documentation, or refining developer workflows, I work hard to raise the floor so that every engineer can contribute at their best. Great teams aren't just built on individual talent but on the systems and support that help everyone thrive. By investing in people as much as in code, we can ensure long-term success for both the team and the software we create.

highlights: Developed automation tools, including custom microservices and machine learning-powered AWS Lambda functions, significantly improving internal workflows. In one case study, reduced task processing time from 2.5 hours per document to just 1 minute.
Designed, built, and maintained a high-performance Excel plugin, now used by thousands of employees at leading global fund managers.
Engineered scalable, high-quality features to extract and transform a dataset encompassing over $29 trillion in assets, enhancing data accessibility and analysis.
Established foundational best practices for codebase architecture, API design, data security, and employee onboarding, scaling the company from a 3-person startup to a 180-employee enterprise.

Led an overhaul of our codebase to prepare for a security audit, making over 26,000 individual improvements across 2,134 files over a 2-month period in order to prevent XSS, CSRF, and SQL injection attacks.
Delivered features for high-profile clients such as Intel and Amazon in .NET, C#, and ColdFusion.

projects.name: WordTree
description: WordTree is a word puzzle played one letter at a time. Players fill a tree of five rows, from a one-letter word at the top to a five-letter word at the bottom, without knowing which letter comes next.

First built in 2023 as an experiment in cross-platform development, the original grew to over 1,000 active users. In 2026 I did a ground-up rewrite for iOS and Android with a shared Daily Puzzle, an Endless mode, live head-to-head duels, verified leaderboards, and replays.

Under the hood, a deterministic TypeScript engine runs unmodified on the phone and in a Cloudflare Worker, so the server can replay every move to verify scores. That one property powers the anti-cheat, multiplayer fairness, and replays. Give it a try!

projects.name: Lex
description: Lex is a wordbuilding roguelike that combines Scrabble and Poker into one experience. Players spell words to score points, then craft synergies and stack absurd multipliers to survive an escalating gauntlet of Bosses.

With over 100 unique Editors that bend the rules, 14 starting Bags, and tile upgrades like Steel, Glass, and Stone, no two runs play the same. Spelling a word is easy. Breaking the dictionary is where the fun begins.

colophon.heading: How this site is made
colophon.tagline: This website redesigns itself every Monday.
paragraphs: Every week a GitHub Action rolls the dice: a design style, a color palette, a type pairing, a layout, a motion personality, and one wildcard rule. Then it hands the result to Gemini along with a $10 budget and a single empty folder.

Gemini builds a brand-new site from scratch, but it isn't allowed to write a single word. Every sentence here comes from one data file that I maintain, and an automated checker rejects the design if even one heading isn't in it.

If the new design passes its checks (accessibility, working links, no invented text, and a security review), it goes live on its own. If it wants to install new packages, it waits for my approval first.
The first time you visit after a new design ships, a timeline flashes through the whole archive, from the original hand-built site up to this one.
